Ambush Bait is a passable method of subjecting low level characters to real danger in a controlled environment. Have the party controlling or riding inside a target vehicle. The initial wave of attack should represent a real danger to the party. After the second or third round of combat the reinforcements should show up and quickly resolve the issue. Added at the beginning of a campaign this can be a good grinder scenario or way to powerlevel the players.

The markets and shops of Srelub revolve around imported goods from distant lands. Some less scrupulous traders will attempt to sneak goods into the city through the slums and shantytowns in an effort to avoid excise taxes or import illicit cargo. When traders dare go where the watch will not hijacking, theft, and murder are real possibilities. While the city council would prefers taxing all imports and hanging smugglers it cannot accept word of "Murdered Merchants", "Slain Sellers", or "Kidnapped Caravans" sullying its reputation as a premier trading hub. To this end it has selected some of the most promising, and expendable, city watch guards to pose as wayward merchants.

The teams of bedraggled mules pull three carts through the narrow passageways of the southern slum. Tires splash polluted water on the feet of four merchants, rough cloth cloaks covering finer coats and jackets. As they cross a bridge over an open sewage drain the beggars on either side of the bridge form a blockade. The rear merchant looks back to see the trailing guard break at least a 30 second run away. So it begins.

Assign the party a role in Tracking and eventually Capturing a Fugitive. If you want to go a step further have the party join the organization and bring down the mob from within, you can even go a step further by having a mole inside the city watch (recently watched The Departed).

In past games when I was the player these scenarios made me feel attached with my party and characters.
